cards.text: Ahab, king of Israel, has done more evil in the LORD's sight than every king before him, and he's serving Baal (1 Kings 16:30-31). Then Elijah the Tishbite, one of the settlers of Gilead, walks right up to the king. No intro, no warm-up, friend: he's got something to say.

cards.question: Elijah is standing in front of King Ahab. What does he tell him?

answers.text: No dew or rain except at his word
No harvest until Ahab tears down his altar
An army will soon surround Samaria

cards.question: Elijah swears this to Ahab by Baal, the god Ahab serves.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Elijah to leave, turn east, and hide himself by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan. And hiding, friend, I could teach a CLASS on, after all my years in the junk drawer.

cards.question: Out at the Brook of Cherith, Elijah can drink the water. But what does the LORD say He's commanded to feed him there?

cards.text: So Elijah does what the LORD said and goes to live by the brook. Then here come the ravens, flying in like room service with WINGS.

cards.question: Every morning and evening, the ravens bring Elijah ___ and ___.

cards.text: Elijah's got water and twice-a-day deliveries, living the quiet life. Then some time later, the Brook of Cherith dries up.

cards.question: Why does the Brook of Cherith dry up?

answers.text: There's been no rain in the land

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Elijah again. Get up, go to Zarephath of Sidon, and stay there.

cards.question: In Zarephath, the LORD says He has commanded a ___ to provide for Elijah.

cards.text: So Elijah goes to Zarephath, and at the city gate there's a widow gathering sticks. Elijah calls out to her.

cards.question: Elijah's last home was a brook that dried up. What does he ask the widow for first?

answers.text: A little water in a cup
A place to stay the night

cards.text: As she heads off to get it, Elijah calls after her with one more request. That's me in the bakery: "Grab me the sprinkles, friend, and while you're UP…"

cards.question: What else does Elijah ask the widow to bring him?

cards.text: The widow stops. As surely as the LORD his God lives, she tells Elijah, she has no bread.

cards.question: The widow has only a handful of ___ in a jar and a little ___ in a jug.
The widow tells Elijah she's gathering sticks to sell at the city gate.

cards.text: "Do not be afraid," Elijah tells her, and he says to go and do as she said. But first, he has one more ask.

cards.question: Before the widow makes a meal for herself and her son, what does Elijah ask her to do?

answers.text: Make him a small cake of bread
Pour him some of her oil
Give him the flour to keep

cards.question: Making Elijah's cake first is a lot to ask with that little flour. Why does Elijah say she'll still have enough?

answers.text: The LORD says her flour and oil won't run out
The ravens will bring her more food
Her neighbors will share what they have

cards.text: So she goes and does exactly what Elijah said. If somebody asked for my LAST scoop of cookie dough, friend, I'd need a minute, a chair and somebody to fan me.

cards.question: From then on, Elijah eats every day, but the widow and her son have to make do with less.

cards.text: That jar of flour never runs out and that jug of oil never runs dry, just like the LORD said through Elijah. Me? I've got a cookie jar that's EMPTY by noon, and I'm the only one who lives here.
Later, the widow's son gets sick. His sickness grows worse and worse, until no breath is left in him.

cards.question: The widow turns to Elijah. What does she ask him?

answers.text: If he came to remind her of her sin
Why the LORD let the drought go on
If he would leave her house for good

cards.text: Elijah says to her, "Give me your son." He takes the boy from her arms and carries him up to the upper room where he's staying.

cards.question: Up in the upper room, Elijah lays the widow's son down on the floor.

cards.text: Then Elijah cries out to the LORD: "O LORD my God, have You also brought tragedy on this widow who has opened her home to me, by causing her son to die?"

cards.question: Elijah stretches himself out over the widow's son and cries out to the LORD again. What does he ask for?

answers.text: For the boy's life to return to him
For his own life in the boy's place
For the LORD to show him the reason

cards.question: Elijah stretches himself out over the child ___ times.
The LORD listens to the voice of Elijah, and the widow's son lives.

cards.text: Elijah carries the boy down from the upper room and gives him to his mother. "Look, your son is alive," Elijah declares.

cards.question: Now the widow tells Elijah she knows something. What is it?

answers.text: He's a man of God who speaks the LORD's truth
The drought will be over very soon
Her son will never get sick again

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. The sky's still shut tight, and trust me, this story is just getting started.

findings.problem: The joke compares Elijah hiding by the Brook of Cherith to Papa Dorin's years in the junk drawer. Papa Dorin wasn't hiding in the drawer. He was put away and forgotten, so the comparison doesn't share the core action of hiding. The sentence 'And hiding, friend, I could teach a CLASS on' is also awkward and doesn't land instantly.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The widow's actual plan in 1 Kings 17:12 is never told on any card: she is gathering sticks to make a last meal for herself and her son 'so that we may eat it and die.' Card 9 only gives a false statement about selling sticks, so a baker who answers it right still never learns her real situation. Card 10 then says Elijah tells her to 'go and do as she said,' which points back to something the baker was never told.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The LORD's promise in 1 Kings 17:14 lasts 'until the day the LORD sends rain upon the face of the earth.' No card tells this time limit. The right answer reduces it to the flour and oil won't run out, and card 15 never mentions it either. The detail ties the miracle to the drought that drives this story group.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Whether Elijah lays the boy on the floor or on his bed is a minor detail that doesn't move the passage forward, and the baker can only get it by luck. Stop 3 already has another pure-detail discovery question (card 7, three times) and an unguessable card 2, so luck-based picks pile up in this stop.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The story cards in stop 3 (1, 3, 5, 9) are bare retellings with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Holding back during the boy's death fits the moment. But the reunion in 1 Kings 17:23 is a moment of joy that can carry his warmth or a laugh, and card 9 reads as plain narration.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
